title: From the Prophet-5 to the Take 5
intro: The Take 5 is Sequential’s compact five-voice polysynth, built on the platform of the 2020 Prophet-5 Rev4 reissue. It keeps the Prophet’s idea, two oscillators and a resonant low-pass filter in each of five voices, and adds what a modern compact poly has: morphing wave shapes, a sub-oscillator, a mod matrix, an arpeggiator and sequencer, and digital effects.

timeline.name: Sequential Circuits Prophet-5
timeline.text: Five voices of two oscillators each, and the first synthesizer that stored every setting of a sound in memory. The Take 5’s five voices, two oscillators and sync from Oscillator 2 to Oscillator 1 come from here.

timeline.name: Sequential Prophet-5 Rev4
timeline.text: A recreation of the original Prophet-5, with two VCOs per voice and switchable filters from the earlier revisions. The Take 5 shares its platform.

timeline.name: Sequential Take 5
timeline.text: Five analogue voices with a 44-key keyboard: two VCOs whose SHAPE morphs from sine to pulse, a sub-oscillator, a resonant low-pass filter with drive, two envelopes with switchable routing, two LFOs, a 16-slot mod matrix, overdrive, one of eleven effects plus reverb, an arpeggiator and a 64-step sequencer.

relatives.name: Oberheim TEO-5
relatives.text: Built on the same platform with the same front-panel layout, with an SEM-style filter that morphs between low-pass, notch and high-pass in place of the Take 5’s low-pass.

relatives.name: Sequential Fourm
relatives.text: A smaller four-voice Sequential poly with a Prophet-5-derived 4-pole filter and polyphonic aftertouch.

relatives.name: Behringer PRO-800
relatives.text: Another affordable route to the Prophet sound: a copy of the 1982 Prophet-600, which this app also plays.

note: None of the databank’s records name the Take 5 yet.
